mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0% regimes, or IC > 0.05 over a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets labor market softening as a signal of potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases then decreases over the next 2 months
failure_condition: IC < -0.1 over 60-day horizon in 70% of such labor signal events, or no significant return difference vs. opposite pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above the prior quarter's peak, sustained for two months, precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent inflationary pressure and tighter policy anticipation.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >60% of such CPI spikes, or IC > 0.08 over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it suggests weakening supply constraints and improved market confidence.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >70% of INDPRO < -2% events, or IC < -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as markets anticipate easing and reinvestment opportunities.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-positive in >80% of such events, or IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining job openings (not directly in catalog but proxy via PAYEMS) coupled with rising pay growth (implied via HOUST) predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softening supports rate cut expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases while HOUST increases over 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market softening with wage growth
failure_condition: IC < -0.15 over 60 days in 50% of such labor signals.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation drop in retail sales proxy (not in catalog but must use available proxies - here using GDPC1 as a demand proxy) in the prior 10 days precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals demand weakness and potential policy restraint.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1 SD over last 10 days
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >70% of such demand drops, or IC > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle regime (regime_hint), a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return occurs when the 1-month change in UNRATE is positive, regardless of other signals, as investors anticipate future rate cuts after peak.
candidate_trigger: any regime and UNRATE monthly change > 0%
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 in >90% of UNRATE up events during tightening regimes.
